title: Mandatory fuel price reporting (Tasmania)
summary: A code of practice made on 1 September 2020 required Tasmanian fuel retailers to register within 14 days and then report each price change within 30 minutes for publication.

instruments.title: Australian Consumer Law (Tasmania) (Code of Practice for Fuel Price Reporting) Regulations 2020
instruments.provisions: Code clauses 2-3: registration within 14 days; reporting within 30 minutes of a price change

commenced.what: Regulations took effect on notification in the Gazette

direction_rationale: Real-time public price data lower motorists' search costs, which should narrow retail margins, but they also let rival retailers see each other's prices at once, which can make tacit coordination and price cycles easier to sustain.
comparison: Staggered adoption 2016-2025. WA (FuelWatch, reporting since 2001) is always treated; the ACT has no mandatory scheme (a voluntary FuelCheck pilot from November 2022, not checked); states not yet reporting at each date.
confounders: crude oil and terminal gate price movements
temporary halving of fuel excise (30 Mar to 28 Sep 2022)
notes: Retailers trading at commencement had 14 days to register, so reporting was in full effect by mid-September 2020.

verified.notes: Read on the Tasmanian register: notified 1 September 2020 and took effect that day.
